body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 61daa2a2af52648c5b2e3fae690c8ac664a9de5c -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code of three posts.

### What is good

- The same-tool rule in the three posts agrees with `tormach.cps` (#1626). The first section always changes or names its tool, because `loadedTool` starts as `null`.
- `xyUnknown` stays `true` after a kept tool. The first traverse still comes after a Z-only rapid to the clearance (#1616). `each_traverse_states_its_height` pins this for all three posts.
- The kept-tool branch in TinyG writes no M5 / M9 again. The section end of the previous section already wrote them. G17 G90 and the WCS word are still written before the branch.
- Grbl 1.1 now counts `toolsLoaded` only for a real load. The first-load comment `LOAD T.. AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START` stays correct.
- A setup change stops by default (`posting_setup_change.rs`, Pause / OptionalStop). That stop sets the tool to unknown, so a re-clamp also asks for the tool again.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/3445-grbl-same-tool.md` says why the Z lift and the spindle words stay.
- No recorded golden changed. This agrees with "Goldens moved: None".

### Results (trial merge with upstream/main `6e641dac7` merged at head `61daa2a2a`, locally)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 58 steps, 0 failed (11.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Extra suites run:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored.
  - `post suites: setup_change, script_grbl, script_grblhal, script_tinyg, grbl_dialect`: all pass.
  - `app suites: after_op, grblhal_post, tinyg_post`: all pass.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on this head: 8 steps, 0 failed (release build plus `app heavy: conformance, control_comp, post_cycle_feed_spindle, probe_no_coolant, program_units, tinyg_post, wear_comp`).

### Mutations that I ran

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `tinyg.cps` from upstream/main | red: the two `tinyg_*` tests |
| Grbl 1.1: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `stop` arm | red: `grbl_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` |
| All three posts: `loadedTool = null` removed from the `optional-stop` arm | **green**: all 6 tests, and the post and app suites above |

### Requested before merge

1. The optional-stop reset has no pinning test: `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:499`, `assets/posts/grbl.cps:503` and `assets/posts/tinyg.cps:531`. If this reset goes, the operator can change the tool at an `M1`. The next same-tool section then writes no `T M6` (no `M0` on Grbl 1.1), and the program cuts with a tool that the post did not ask for. This is a silent wrong program. Add an `optional-stop` case to each `*_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` test in `crates/post/tests/grbl_family_same_tool.rs`. For example: `post(s, m, &[(1, "optional-stop"), (1, "")])` gives `["T1 M6", "T1 M6"]` for grblHAL and TinyG, and on Grbl 1.1 one `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T1` note with its `M0` after the `M1`. Then do the mutation again and name it in the body.

### Notes (not blocking)

- The `optionalStop` post option (the `M1` before a tool change) is now also not written for a kept tool. The body says this for grblHAL. This is correct: no tool change occurs.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
